blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Sparse inertial pose estimation promises camera-free motion capture from consumer devices, but consumer sensors are unreliable: firmware-fused orientations are biased, mounting varies between sessions, and streams drift or drop out. On a new 35-take single-subject benchmark pairing an earbud head inertial measurement unit (IMU) with two smart-insole foot IMUs (SAM-3D-Body pseudo-ground-truth labels), we show the reliability problem is channel-level: a channel ablation isolates foot acceleration as the most informative input (66.6 mm vs. 79.0 mm head-only) and the firmware-fused foot orientation as the liability that destroys the gain. We therefore let the model learn how much to trust each channel of each stream: one temporal gate per stream per channel block, trained with an auxiliary reliability objective on synthetically corrupted pretraining data. The channel-gated model is the most accurate of our learned fusion arms on clean data (69.4 mm vs. 83.7 static, 86.6 ungated) and under every simulated fault (bias in training; drift, dropout eval-only); its gates suppress the natively biased foot-orientation channels on clean real data without test-time supervision and flag dropout bursts at 0.92–0.999 AUROC. Two contrasts: dropping a channel known a priori to fail is flat across foot faults but collapses when an unanticipated stream fails (head dropout: 92.9 vs. 79.3 mm); and a fine-tuned HMD-Poser is more accurate on clean data (64.4 mm) and nominally under drift, with no significant paired difference under bias or dropout, but a larger worst-case degradation from clean ( + 16.1 +16.1 vs. + 3.5 +3.5 mm, single seed). Learning to gate reliability instead of sensor count is the lever for deployable sparse inertial capture. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhilinGuo/reliability-gated-imu-fusion .
blocks.zh: Sparse惯性提出了来自消费设备的无相机运动捕捉的估计承诺,但消费传感器是不可靠的:固件喷射方向有偏颇,各会间上升,溪流漂移或退出. 在一个新的35摄制单主体基准上,将一个耳罩头惯性测量单元(IMU)与两个智能插入脚式IMU(SAM-3D-Body伪地面-真伪标签)配对,我们显示可靠性问题在于信道级别:一个信道衰减隔离脚步加速,作为信息最丰富的输入(66.6毫米对79.0毫米只头)和固件充足方向作为破坏收益的责任。 因此,我们让模型学习如何相信每条流的每个通道:每个流的每个通道块一个时间门,在合成腐烂的预训数据上训练一个辅助可靠性目标. 我们所学的关于清洁数据的聚变武器(69.4毫米对83.7静态,86.6升格)和每个模拟断层(训练中的比方;漂流,退学的仅限等)中最准确的就是这种信道;它的大门压制了当地对清洁真实数据有偏见的脚指向渠道,没有试验时的监督,而且旗的失落在0.92-0.999 AUROC。 两种对比: 投放已知先验失败的通道在足部断层之间是平的,但在意外的溪流失败时是倒塌的(头部断层:92.9对79.3毫米); 微调的HMD-Poser在清洁数据(64.4毫米)上更准确,名义上在漂流下更准确,在偏差或辍学的情况下没有显著的对等差异,而是比清洁更严重的退化(+16.1+16.1对+3.5+3.5毫米,单种). 学会门的可靠性而不是感应计数是可部署的稀疏惯性捕捉的杠杆. 代码见https://github.com/ZhilinGuo/可靠性-gated-imu-musion。 。 。 。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Sparse wearable pose estimation promises camera-free avatar control, motion entertainment, and at-home gait analysis: once trained, an inertial model needs no cameras at deployment. Yet most published systems assume a six-IMU suit, a pelvis or back tracker, and research-grade sensors with raw gyroscopes [ 13 , 34 , 33 , 16 ] . We instead target a configuration built entirely from consumer devices (Fig. 1 ): one head IMU from earbuds (AirPods) and two foot IMUs from smart insoles (Striv). The layout suits gait and lower-body motion: feet observe stance, swing, and contact; the head provides a stable orientation reference. But it breaks two assumptions the literature relies on: there is no pelvis/root sensor, so root translation and hip axial rotation are weakly observed; and the insole firmware emits a fused Euler orientation with no raw gyroscope, so calibration error cannot be removed by gyro-based filtering.
blocks.zh: Sparse可穿戴预估保证无相机的Avatar控制,运动娱乐,以及家用步态分析:一旦经过训练,惯性模型在部署时不需要相机. 然而,大多数已公布的系统都假定一种6-IMU套装、盆盖或背跟踪器以及带有原陀螺仪的研究级传感器[13、34、33、16]。 相反,我们的目标是完全由消费装置(图1)建造的配置:一个头来自耳机(AirPods)的IMU,两个脚来自智能的Insoles(Striv)的IMU. 布局适合步法和下体运动:脚观察姿势,摆动,和接触;头部提供稳定的定向参考. 但是它打破了文献所依赖的两个假设:没有骨盆/根传感器,因此根翻译和臀部轴旋转的观测能力很弱;而无孔固件释放出一个没有原始陀螺仪的引信的Euler方向,因此校准错误不能通过陀螺仪的滤波来清除.

blocks.en: With neither marker-based mocap nor hardware synchronization, we treat label generation and alignment as first-class system problems. Cameras are required at training time only: vision is the teacher, not the input; the one deployment-time vision dependency is per-take mounting calibration, isolated and bounded in Sec. 6.4 . We capture four-view RGB-D video alongside the wearables, align modalities after the fact by motion agreement [ 17 ] , and generate pseudo-ground-truth (pseudo-GT) with SAM 3D Body [ 32 ] . We then benchmark an IMUPoser-style recurrent model [ 21 ] pretrained on synthetic AMASS IMU [ 20 ] and fine-tuned on our pseudo-GT.
blocks.zh: 由于既不是基于标记的mocap,也不是硬件同步,我们把标签生成和对齐视为一级系统问题. 只在培训时需要照相机:视线是老师,而不是输入;一次部署时视线的依赖性是每次升降校准、隔离和在Sec定界。 6.4 (英语). 我们捕捉四景的 RGB-D 视频, 与可穿戴的, 然后我们以IMUPoser式的经常型号为基准,在合成AMASS IMU[20]上预先训练,并在我们的伪GT上进行微调。

blocks.en: This paper extends a preliminary workshop pilot [ 7 ] on the same takes, which reported that adding the foot IMUs degrades pose below a head-only model. On the corrected pipeline the penalty shrinks below detectability on held-out runs (80.3 vs. 79.0 mm sim-MPJPE; paired per-take median + 1.8 +1.8 mm, p = 0.41 p{=}0.41 ). A channel ablation reveals a sharp internal structure: foot acceleration alone is the best input configuration we test (66.6 mm, significantly better than head-only), foot orientation alone is worse than no feet on average (marginally so two-sided, p = 0.054 p{=}0.054 ), and adding the orientation channels to the acceleration channels destroys most of the gain (Hodges–Lehmann + 12.9 +12.9 mm, p < 10 − 5 p{<}10^{-5} ). The prize and the toxin arrive in the same stream. Since deployment faults are unknown a priori and time-varying, the research question shifts from “how many sensors?” to “how much should each channel of each sensor be trusted, and when?”
blocks.zh: 本文将初步讲习班试点[7]扩展至相同的取材,其中报告说,添加脚部IMU降解后形成一个单头模型。 在经过纠正的输油管上,阻断运行时的可探测性以下的罚则缩小(80.3对79.0毫米sim-MPJPE;每摄取中位数+1.8+1.8毫米,p=0.41p=0.41p=0.41)。 一个通道加速揭示出一个尖锐的内部结构:单脚加速是我们测试的最佳输入配置(66.6毫米,明显优于只头),单脚定向比平均没有脚更差(边缘如此双侧,p=0.054 p{=}0.054),加速度通道的定向通道破坏大部分收益(Hodges–Lehmann + 12.9 + 12.9 mm,p < 10 - 5 p{<}10^{-5}). 奖品和毒素到达同一溪流. 由于部署断层是不为人所知的先验和时间变化,研究问题从“多少传感器?” 转移到“每个传感器的每个信道应相信多少? 何时? “

blocks.en: Our answer is channel-reliability gating : each channel block (orientation, acceleration) of each stream is weighted by a scalar gate with a short temporal receptive field, trained with an auxiliary reliability objective during corruption-augmented pretraining. The channel gate is the best learned fusion arm on clean data and under all four simulated fault regimes, and its gates are interpretable without test-time supervision: on clean real data they partially close on the natively biased foot-orientation channels, they close further when bias enters the fine-tuning distribution, and they react online to burst faults. A control trained without the auxiliary objective leaves gates high and unselective on the same clean data: the selectivity is transferred from synthetic-corruption supervision, not emergent from the task loss. Stream-level gates add little over static learned weights, an honest negative result that localizes the benefit at channel granularity.
blocks.zh: 我们的答案是频道可靠性:每条流的每个频道块(定向,加速度)都由一个具有短暂时间可接受场的scalar门进行加权,在腐败强化预训中以辅助可靠性目标训练. 信道闸门是在清洁数据和所有四个模拟断层系统下最有知识的聚变臂,它的闸门可以在没有测试时间监督的情况下解释:在清洁的真实数据上,它们部分关闭在本土偏颇的脚指向信道上,当偏差进入微调分布时,它们会进一步关闭,它们在网上对破裂的断层作出反应. 在没有辅助目标的情况下经过训练的管制使闸门高而无选择性地存放在同一清洁数据上:选择性是从合成腐败监督中转移出来的,而不是从任务损失中转移出来的。 流层的闸门很少增加静态的学习权重,这是一个诚实的负面结果,它使好处在通道颗粒性上本地化.

blocks.en: Contributions. • A 35-take single-subject consumer-IMU benchmark (4 × \times RGB-D + earbud head IMU + two insole IMUs) with released capture, after-the-fact alignment, and pseudo-GT labeling protocols, and run/motion held-out evaluation with similarity-aligned, distal, and temporal metrics. • A controlled channel-level diagnosis of consumer foot IMUs: foot acceleration alone is the best input configuration (66.6 mm), foot orientation alone is toxic, and a monotone dose–response isolates orientation bias, not sensor count, as the cause. • Channel-reliability gating: one temporal gate per stream per channel block with corruption-supervised pretraining, the most accurate learned-fusion arm on clean data and under all fault regimes (69.4 / 77.8 / 69.6 / 72.8 mm clean/bias/drift/dropout, three seeds; sign-consistent in 7 / 7 7/7 classes); gates suppress the natively biased channels without test-time supervision and flag dropout bursts at 0.92–0.999 AUROC. • A deployment analysis bounding the design space: a priori channel drop vs. learned gating under anticipated and unanticipated faults, an external HMD-Poser comparison at 4.6 × 4.6\times CPU throughput with 37 % 37\% fewer parameters, and negative results for one-time T-pose calibration, oracle hard masking, and augmentation without gating.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Sparse-IMU full-body pose. Sparse-IMU reconstruction progressed from offline optimization over a statistical body model [ 28 ] through learning-based six-IMU pipelines [ 13 ] , real-time physics-aware optimization [ 34 , 33 ] , Transformers [ 16 ] , diverse-real-data generalization [ 35 ] , and diffusion from arbitrary sensor sets including pressure insoles [ 27 ] . These define the methodological backbone but assume a pelvis sensor and raw gyroscopes.
blocks.zh: Sparse-IMU 全身姿势. Sparse-IMU重建从离线优化到统计体模型[28],通过基于学习的6-IMU管道[13],实时物理认知优化[34,33],变形器[16],多元-真实数据概括[35],以及从包括压力溶液在内的任意传感器集传播[27]. 这些定义了方法主干线,但假设了骨盆传感器和原始陀螺仪.

blocks.en: Commodity-device and VR sparse tracking. IMUPoser, our primary baseline for its transparency and earbud relevance, estimates pose from variable phone/watch/earbud subsets [ 21 ] ; MobilePoser targets 1–3 mobile IMUs [ 29 ] , ProgIP uses three IMUs at head and wrists [ 38 ] , and IMUCoCo conditions on continuous on-body coordinates [ 36 ] . VR trackers infer full-body motion from head-and-hands input [ 15 , 5 , 14 , 30 ] ; HMD-Poser scales to HMD plus a few IMUs with pretrained HMD+2IMU weights [ 3 ] . These observe the upper body and hallucinate the legs, the inverse of our feet-informed setting; none places sensors at head plus both feet.
blocks.zh: 商品设备 和 VR 零星跟踪。 IMUPoser是我国提高透明度和耳罩关联性的主要基线,它从可变电话/监视/耳罩子集中得出的估计数[21];移动 Poser目标 1–3 移动式IMU [29],ProgIP在头部和手腕上使用三个IMU [38],IMUCoCo条件在连续的机体坐标上使用[36]. VR跟踪器从头和手输入中推断出全身运动[15,5,14,30];HMD-Poser比例尺到HMD+少数具有预训HMD+2IMU重量的IMU [3]. 这些观察者观察上身,并幻觉腿部, 反向的我们了解脚的设置; 没有将传感器置于头部和双脚。

blocks.en: Foot/insole sensing and clinical gait. Reduced-IMU lower-limb estimation recovers walking kinematics from two or three IMUs at ∼ 6 {\sim}6 cm segment error while degrading on turns and dynamic motion [ 26 , 9 ] ; GRIP fuses insole pressure with a physics digital twin [ 10 ] ; wearables see growing use in Parkinsonian gait assessment [ 6 ] . This literature both motivates feet and predicts where they fail.
blocks.zh: 脚/分子感知和临床动作。 减低的IMU低高度估计从2或3个IMU中恢复了行走动动因子,时间为 6 {\sim}6 cm 段误差,同时在转弯和动态运动中降解 [26,9];GRIP用物理数字双双 [10] 诱导独行压力;可穿戴器在Parkinsonian gait 评估中使用的越来越多 [6]. 这种文献既能激发脚步的动力,又能预测它们失败的地方.

blocks.en: Robustness and gating. Sensor faults are an emerging concern: TIC learns dynamic on-body calibration [ 39 ] , MagShield hardens against magnetic disturbance [ 23 ] , UMotion propagates inertial+ultra-wideband (UWB) uncertainty [ 18 ] , and WHIP, the closest concurrent work, reconstructs motion from consumer wearables including instrumented insoles, but with raw IMU channels and hardware-synchronized mocap supervision [ 2 ] . Our setting is complementary and harsher: consumer fused orientations whose bias is not identifiable under the training distribution, faults that appear only at test time, and a gate that must infer reliability from the stream itself. Gating is classical for modality fusion [ 1 , 24 , 8 , 11 , 22 , 25 ] ; we claim no new mechanism; the contribution is its instantiation and validation for test-time sensor faults in inertial capture, where the reliability signal must come from the faulty stream itself.
blocks.zh: 强健与吉祥. 传感器断层是一个新出现的关切:TIC学习动态机体校准[39],MagShield硬度防磁扰动[23],UMotion传播惯性+超宽波段(UWB)不确定性[18],而WHIP作为最密切的并行工作,从消费者的可穿戴器中重建运动,包括仪器溶液,但有原始的IMU通道和硬件同步模具监督[2]. 我们所处的环境是互补的、更严酷的:消费者的结合方向,在培训分配下其偏差无法辨别,缺陷只在试验时出现,以及必须从溪流本身推断可靠性的大门。 Gating是模式聚变的经典[1,24,8,11,22,25];我们声称没有新的机制;贡献在于它在惯性捕捉中的测试时间传感器故障的即时化和验证,其中可靠性信号必须来自故障流本身.

blocks.en: Vision+IMU fusion and pseudo-GT. DeepFuse, the closest WACV precedent, fuses body-worn IMUs with multi-view images [ 12 ] ; pose-based multi-view alignment removes hardware sync [ 4 ] . We use vision only to create labels: SAM 3D Body for pseudo-GT [ 32 , 31 ] , AMASS for synthetic pretraining [ 20 ] , motion agreement for alignment [ 17 ] . To our knowledge no prior work benchmarks our layout: head + two feet, no pelvis, no foot gyro.
blocks.zh: 视觉+IMU聚变和伪GT. DeepFuse, WACV 最近的先例, 引信 body-worn IMU 与多视图图像 [12] ; 基于姿势的多视图对齐删除硬件同步 [4]. 我们只使用视觉来创建标签: SAM 3D 伪GT机体[32,31],合成预训的AMASS[20],对齐的运动协议[17]. 据我们所知,没有前期工作的基准 我们的布局:头+两英尺,没有骨盆,没有脚陀螺。

blocks.en: 3 Capture, Alignment, and Pseudo-Ground-Truth
blocks.zh: 3 捕捉、对齐和Pseudo-Ground-Truth

blocks.en: The capture rig comprises four Intel RealSense RGB-D cameras ( 848 × 480 848\times 480 at 30 FPS, color + depth), one AirPods head IMU streamed via a custom iOS app (fused attitude, device-frame linear acceleration, gyroscope), and left/right Striv insole IMUs (fused Euler orientation plus acceleration, no raw gyroscope, ∼ 30 {\sim}30 Hz over BLE). The motion protocol is five repeated runs of seven scripts (35 takes; supp. S1) spanning standing and straight walking with 180 ∘ 180^{\circ} turns, in-place stepping and single-leg stance, side-steps/grapevine/ 360 ∘ 360^{\circ} turns, squats/bends/lunges/sit-to-stand, an everyday walk–sit–pick-up composite, clinical gait (abrupt stop/restart, dual-task), and upper-limb reaches and strikes. The protocol is intentionally dual-use, covering clinical gait and turning as well as avatar-oriented composite motion.

blocks.en: Dataset statistics. The benchmark contains 82,417 frames (45.8 minutes at 30 FPS) across the 35 takes (mean 78.5 s, range 38.6–137.1 s). SAM 3D Body yields a usable nine-joint lower-body label for every frame; each foot is in ground contact for 65% of frames (73% for at least one foot). Each take stores aligned head and foot orientation matrices and accelerations (and head gyro, used only for alignment and in one ablation arm), the nine lower-body joints, a 70-joint Momentum-Human-Rig pose, per-foot contacts, a global root rotation, and a validity mask. Human-subjects statement: the single subject is an author who self-captured with informed consent; no identifiable imagery is published.
blocks.zh: 数据集统计. 该基准包含82,417个框架(30 FPS时45.8分钟),涵盖35项(平均78.5秒,范围为38.6至137.1秒)。 萨姆3D 身体为每个帧产生一个可用的九联下体标签;每只脚在地面接触65%的帧(至少1英尺为73%). 每个库都采用对齐头部和脚部方向矩阵和加速度(和头陀螺旋,仅用于对齐和在一个割裂臂内),9个下体关节,一个70-联动的Momentum-Human-Rig姿势,每英尺接触,一个全球根旋转,以及一个有效性罩. 人主体声明:单主体是作者在知情同意下自行捕捉;没有公布可识别图像.

blocks.en: Temporal alignment. We have no hardware sync, only Unix-style timestamps with constant offsets and slow drift. We resample all streams onto a common 30 Hz grid, then estimate two offsets. The head offset cross-correlates AirPods gyro magnitude against head angular speed derived from SAM orientation, following motion-agreement temporal calibration [ 17 ] . A shared foot offset (the insoles share one BLE base station and clock) cross-correlates Striv motion intensity against SAM foot speed over the whole take. The full-dataset offsets ( − 2.69 ± 0.06 -2.69{\pm}0.06 s head, − 3.05 ± 0.10 -3.05{\pm}0.10 s feet) are consistent with the expected clock skew, and excluding the six takes whose head-alignment confidence falls below 0.5 0.5 leaves every headline conclusion unchanged (supp. S1).
blocks.zh: 时间调整。 我们没有硬件同步,只有Unix风格的时标有恒定偏移和缓慢漂移. 我们把所有的溪流重新做成一个30Hz的通用网格,然后估计两个抵消. 头部在运动-协议时间校准[17]后,抵消了AirPods陀螺仪对来自SAM方向的头角速度的交叉角. 共享的足部偏移(英索尔人共享一个BLE基站和时钟) 跨锥体的斯特里夫运动强度与SAM的足部速度相比整个摄取. 完整的数据集抵消(− 2.69± 0.06-2.69~pm}0.06 s head,− 3.05± 0.10~3.05~pm}0.10 s feet)与预期的时钟skew一致,不包括其头部对齐置信度低于0.5 0.5的6个头条结论不变(supp.S1)。

blocks.en: Pseudo-ground-truth via SAM 3D Body. For supervision we run SAM 3D Body [ 32 ] on a selected camera view and convert its Momentum-Human-Rig output to a nine-joint lower-body target: pelvis, left/right hip, knee, ankle, and foot (supp. S2). We treat these labels as pseudo-GT with measurable bias rather than mocap-grade truth: single-image recovery is strong on clear standing and walking frames but noisier under self-occlusion, fast motion, and turning. As a label-integrity control, we re-labeled all 35 takes with four-view fused labels (per-view residuals 7.9–27.9 mm, median 15.0) and re-scored the same held-out head-only predictions against both label sets, with no retraining: lower-body error changes by 0.6 0.6 mm (83.9 vs. 84.5 mm; supp. S2), so label view choice does not drive any conclusion. Both label sets derive from the same model family, so this control validates view choice, not absolute label correctness (Sec. 7 ). Each take is spatially calibrated by fitting a constant sensor-to-bone rotation per sensor against that take’s own SAM-derived bone frames over the whole take (a transductive fit; two-sided Procrustes; fitted magnitudes and audits: supp. S1).
blocks.zh: 通过 SAM 3D body 的 Pseudo-ground- truth. 互联网档案馆的存檔,存档日期2013-03-02. 为了监督起见,我们将SAM 3D body [32] 运行在选定的相机视图上,并将它的Momentum-Human-Rig输出转换为9联的下体目标:骨盆,左/右臀,膝盖,脚踝,和脚(supp. S2). 我们把这些标签当作伪GT,以可测量的偏差而不是摩卡普级的真理来对待:单像恢复在清晰的站立和行走框上很强,但在自闭,快速运动,和转弯下却发出噪声. 作为标签集成控制,我们用四视的引信标签(每视残片7.9–27.9毫米,中位数15.0)重新标注了所有35个取材的标签,并重新标注了两个标签组相同的只保留头部的预测,没有再培训:下体误差变化0.6 6毫米(83.9对84.5毫米;supp.S2),所以标签视图选择不会推动任何结论. 两个标签集都来源于同一个模型家族,因此这个控制验证了视图选择,而不是绝对的标签正确性(Sec.7 ). 每件取料在空间上经过校准,每件取料器安装一个恒定的传感器对骨轮转,与取材自成的SAM骨架对接整个取料(转录式取料;双侧推进器;装配尺寸和审计:supp.S1)。

blocks.en: Our model augments an IMUPoser-style recurrent backbone [ 21 ] with a reliability-gated fusion layer (Fig. 2 ). Each IMU contributes linear acceleration and a 3 × 3 3\times 3 orientation matrix, packed as a 12-D per-sensor vector; the full input is 36-D for head-plus-feet, and sensor ablations zero the unused blocks. A two-layer bidirectional LSTM maps the windowed input to 6D rotations [ 37 ] for nine lower-body joints, and forward kinematics with SMPL-style conventions [ 19 ] produces 3D joint positions. We pretrain on synthetic IMU generated from CMU, BioMotionLab NTroje, and MPI HDM05 sequences in AMASS [ 20 ] by placing virtual sensors at the head and both feet (omitting any synthesized foot gyro to match Striv), then fine-tune per fold on real pseudo-GT.
blocks.zh: 我们的模型增加了一个IMUPoser式的经常性主干[21],具有可靠性加成的聚变层(图2)。 每个IMU都贡献线性加速度和一个3×3 3\时的3定向矩阵,包装为每传感器的12D矢量;全输入为36-D头加脚,传感器擦除0未使用的块. 双层双向LSTM将窗口输入映射到9个下体关节的6D旋转[37],与SMPL风格的常规的前进动能[19]生成3D联合位置. 我们通过将虚拟传感器放在头部和双脚上(将任何合成的脚陀螺仪装配到Striv上)来预演由CMU,BioMotionLab NTroje和AMASS [20]中的MPI HDM05序列生成的合成IMU,然后在真实的伪GT上每折叠微调.

blocks.en: Corruption augmentation and gate supervision. Pretraining synthesizes three corruption types on random foot streams with per-window probability 0.5 0.5 : constant bias (a fixed body-frame rotation offset per window), drift (a slowly varying offset), and dropout (bursts of zeroed frames), each accompanied by an indicator c i ​ ( t ) c_{i}(t) . Gates receive an auxiliary binary cross-entropy (BCE) objective (weight 0.1 0.1 ) against per-block reliability 1 − c i , b ​ ( t ) 1-c_{i,b}(t) , where bias and drift mark only the orientation block corrupted and dropout marks both. This supervision applies during pretraining only: on real fine-tuning data the “clean” foot streams are natively biased, and we found that continuing gate supervision there forces gates open against the task loss. Fine-tuning therefore optimizes the aligned-FK position loss alone, with the same corruption augmentation kept active so the gates retain their pretrained selectivity (Sec. 6.3 verifies that this selectivity is transferred from the auxiliary supervision, not emergent from the task loss).

blocks.en: Implementation details. The network is a faithful IMUPoser RNN : per-stream stems, the gated fusion layer, a linear projection to 512 units, a two-layer bidirectional LSTM (512 hidden units per direction, input dropout 0.2), and a linear head to the 9 × 6 = 54 9\times 6=54 -D pose output. Acceleration is globally scaled by 30 ​ m / s 2 30\,\mathrm{m/s^{2}} , matching IMUPoser. Synthetic pretraining uses an ℓ 1 \ell_{1} loss on the 6D rotations, Adam (lr 3 × 10 − 4 3{\times}10^{-4} ), 40 epochs, reaching 6.9 ∘ 6.9^{\circ} mean geodesic error on held-out synthetic motion. Fine-tuning uses 5 s windows (150 frames), batch 32, Adam (lr 1 × 10 − 4 1{\times}10^{-4} ), 20 epochs, evaluating the final checkpoint; the loss is computed in 3D after differentiable forward kinematics under a detached per-window similarity (rotation + scale) alignment, rewarding correct relative lower-body geometry rather than absolute placement.

blocks.en: We evaluate two protocols. Leave-one-run-out (“run”) holds out one of the five repeats and tests on unseen repetitions of seen motions; leave-one-motion-out (“seq”) holds out an entire motion class and is the harder generalization test. All numbers use the full 35-take checkpoint sweep, and we report a constant mean-pose prior and a zero-input control as sanity floors.

blocks.en: The cause is the orientation channel, not the sensor. A channel ablation separates the informative signal from the toxic one (three seeds each; table: supp. S4). On the head stream, orientation alone is insufficient (93.9 mm), orientation+acceleration recovers the head-only result (78.5 mm; cf. 79.0 mm in Table 1 ), and adding the head gyroscope changes nothing (78.7 mm). On the foot streams the split is decisive: foot acceleration only yields the best configuration tested (66.6 mm, HL − 10.7 -10.7 mm vs. the Table 1 head-only model, 95% CI [ − 16.0 , − 6.7 ] [-16.0,-6.7] , p = 1.2 × 10 − 5 p{=}1.2{\times}10^{-5} ), foot orientation only is worse than no feet on average (83.9 mm; HL + 4.8 +4.8 mm [ − 0.0 , + 9.3 ] [-0.0,+9.3] ), though only marginally so two-sided ( p = 0.054 p{=}0.054 ), and adding orientation to acceleration destroys most of the gain (66.6 → \rightarrow 80.3 mm; HL + 12.9 +12.9 mm [ + 8.8 , + 19.3 ] [+8.8,+19.3] , p = 8.7 × 10 − 6 p{=}8.7{\times}10^{-6} ). The prize is foot acceleration, specifically the high-passed world-frame signal (whose world rotation still consumes the uncorrected orientation, supp. S1); the toxin is the firmware-fused foot orientation. A dose–response sweep of injected constant mounting bias degrades the ungated model monotonically on every seed (86.6 to 114.7 mm from σ = 0 ∘ \sigma{=}0^{\circ} to 40 ∘ 40^{\circ} , Spearman ρ = 1.0 \rho{=}1.0 ; supp. S4) [ 26 , 9 ] . When the toxic channel is known a priori, dropping it is robust by construction (orientation faults never reach the model); Sec. 6.4 quantifies what that costs when the other stream fails.

blocks.en: Table 2 compares the six gate instantiations of Sec. 4 against two robustness baselines and an oracle; three findings stand out. (i) Channel-level gating dominates. The channel gate is the best arm in every column (held-out predictions: Fig. 3 ): on clean data it beats the ungated control by 16.8 16.8 mm (Hodges–Lehmann, 95% CI [ 10.8 , 22.4 ] [10.8,22.4] ) and the strongest stream-level variant (static weights) by 11.9 11.9 mm [ 6.6 , 20.4 ] [6.6,20.4] ; under bias, drift, and dropout the HL margins over the ungated model are + 22.1 +22.1 [ 14.9 , 29.7 ] [14.9,29.7] , + 16.6 +16.6 [ 11.2 , 22.8 ] [11.2,22.8] , and + 20.5 +20.5 [ 15.4 , 26.2 ] [15.4,26.2] mm (Holm p < 10 − 6 p{<}10^{-6} each; supp. S4). At script level the margin is sign-consistent in 7 / 7 7/7 classes in every fault regime ( p = 0.016 p{=}0.016 , the n = 7 n{=}7 floor), growing on the seq split ( 79.5 79.5 vs. 100.7 100.7 mm clean, seed s0; supp. S4). (ii) Stream-level gates add little over static weights. Static per-stream weights are the strongest stream-level arm under every fault; the temporal and per-frame learned gates numerically match or trail it, and cross-stream softmax attention, which like static is trained without the auxiliary objective, helps modestly under bias and dropout ( ∼ 5 {\sim}5 mm, untested) but not under drift. The aux reliability objective is what carries selectivity: removing it yields the worst stream-level arm on clean data (89.8 mm, three seeds), and the channel-level variant (single seed) matches clean accuracy (71.7 vs. 71.1 mm) but loses fault robustness (bias σ = 20 ∘ \sigma{=}20^{\circ} : 86.5 vs. 75.0 mm) because its orientation gates never close (supp. S4). A per-frame channel-gate variant under-closes the orientation blocks ( 0.83 0.83 / 0.61 0.61 clean, seed s0) and trails the temporal channel gate in every regime and seed (three-seed means 92.7 92.7 vs. 77.8 77.8 mm under bias σ = 20 ∘ \sigma{=}20^{\circ} , HL + 14.0 +14.0 mm [ + 10.4 , + 18.7 ] [+10.4,+18.7] , p = 9.8 × 10 − 9 p{=}9.8{\times}10^{-9} ): temporal context, not granularity alone, carries the bias signature (supp. S4). (iii) Neither oracle masking nor augmentation alone explains the result. Overriding the per-frame gate with the ground-truth corruption indicator is catastrophic (132.9 mm at bias σ = 20 ∘ \sigma{=}20^{\circ} ): the oracle hard-masks both feet for the whole take, a pattern the trunk never saw in training since dropout augmentation masks only bursts, so test-time masking is a distribution shift. An ungated model with the same corruption augmentation collapses on clean data and under eval-only faults (102.2/100.3/108.3 vs. 86.6/87.6/94.1 mm), helping only under train+test bias, where the fault enters fine-tuning (97.5 vs. 100.5 mm; supp. S4).

blocks.en: The gates are not supervised at test time, yet they distinguish unreliable channels from reliable ones (Fig. 4 ; gallery: supp. S5). On real clean data, with no synthetic corruption at all, the channel gate’s foot-orientation blocks sit at 0.41 0.41 (left) and 0.15 0.15 (right) while every other block stays open ( ≥ 0.99 {\geq}0.99 ). The base selectivity is seeded by the corruption design (bias and drift corrupt only the orientation block; the pretrained gate already partially closes foot orientation on clean synthetic data, 0.66 0.66 / 0.65 0.65 , supp. S4), but on real data the closure deepens and lateralizes under the fine-tuning task loss alone (aux off, augmentation active), matching the channel ablation of Sec. 6.1 ; a stream-level control without the auxiliary objective leaves gates high and unselective on the same data ( 0.81 0.81 / 0.93 0.93 / 0.91 0.91 per stream): the selectivity is transferred from synthetic-corruption supervision, not emergent. The left/right asymmetry ( 0.41 ± 0.10 0.41{\pm}0.10 vs. 0.15 ± 0.04 0.15{\pm}0.04 ) is unexplained by bias magnitude (median | B | |B| 34.3 ∘ 34.3^{\circ} vs. 35.0 ∘ 35.0^{\circ} ): gate value is channel-specific fault structure, not a calibrated scalar. For constant bias the defense is a learned prior, not online estimation: a fixed model holds accuracy nearly flat across eval-only bias σ = 5 ∘ \sigma{=}5^{\circ} – 40 ∘ 40^{\circ} ( 71.2 → 77.8 71.2{\to}77.8 mm) with gates nearly unchanged ( 0.41 → 0.44 0.41{\to}0.44 , seed s0); only bias present in fine-tuning closes them further ( 0.21 0.21 / 0.11 0.11 ), and that model keeps the sharpened prior on clean data too ( 0.21 0.21 / 0.10 0.10 ): the closure is written into the weights (dose–response: supp. S4). Under slow drift the stream-level gate fluctuates with local signal statistics without systematic decay (gallery: supp. S5); the channel gate’s closed orientation prior leaves little to track. For burst faults the response is online and fast: foot-acceleration gates close inside dropout bursts (take-averaged 0.08 0.08 vs. 1.00 1.00 outside, per-take median drop − 0.94 -0.94 ; Fig. 4 b). Zeroed bursts are trivially detectable; the deployment value is one mechanism carrying the native-bias prior and burst response together; the acceleration blocks give 99.5 99.5 – 99.7 % 99.7\% burst recall at 2 2 – 6 % 6\% false positives (AUROC 0.999 0.999 / 0.92 0.92 ; caveats: supp. S4). A gate-triggered hard fallback is slower to recover and less accurate (supp. S4): soft down-weighting, not hard switching, is the right use.

blocks.en: Table 3 places gated fusion against published systems adapted to our data through a deterministic adapter package (supp. S3). HMD-Poser [ 3 ] , a 17.4M-parameter transformer pretrained on full AMASS and fine-tuned per fold under our protocol with its HMD slot fed rotation and rotation velocity only and translational channels zeroed (a handicap; supp. S3), is the most accurate on clean data (64.4 mm) but degrades the most under faults ( + 16.1 +16.1 mm worst-case vs. + 3.5 +3.5 mm for the gate). Paired per-take tests (single seed, exploratory) find HMD-Poser better on clean data (HL − 7.0 -7.0 mm [ − 10.7 , − 2.2 ] [-10.7,-2.2] , p = 0.005 p{=}0.005 ) and under drift ( − 4.7 -4.7 [ − 8.4 , − 0.2 ] [-8.4,-0.2] , p = 0.04 p{=}0.04 ; Bonferroni p = 0.18 p{=}0.18 over the four contrasts), with no significant difference under bias or dropout (HL + 1.8 +1.8 [ − 6.6 , + 15.1 ] [-6.6,+15.1] and − 0.5 -0.5 [ − 4.0 , + 3.8 ] [-4.0,+3.8] mm; p ≥ 0.69 p{\geq}0.69 ). Giving HMD-Poser the same corruption augmentation hurts its clean accuracy (76.2 mm) and helps no regime: its worst-case degradation stays + 5.9 +5.9 mm (vs. + 16.1 +16.1 mm unaugmented and + 3.5 +3.5 mm for the gate). This closes the “just augment the baseline” rebuttal. MobilePoser [ 29 ] zero-shot is insensitive to corruption but inaccurate overall (125.3 mm); fine-tuning under position-only supervision fails (three recipes, all worse than zero-shot), consistent with its two-stage stack requiring intermediate joint supervision to adapt. Ours trades a slice of clean accuracy for the best worst-case accuracy at 4.6 × 4.6\times HMD-Poser’s CPU throughput with 37 % 37\% fewer parameters (supp. S7), the relevant operating point for always-on deployment, where mounting offsets are large by default and faults accumulate. Two caveats: HMD-Poser’s output scale drifts ∼ 34 × {\sim}34\times under our scale-invariant loss, so the similarity alignment absorbs it and its absolute numbers remain optimistic (supp. S3); and its clean-data advantage rests on full-AMASS pretraining (vs. our three subsets).

blocks.en: A priori drop vs. learned gate. The foot-acceleration-only configuration (feet-A; Sec. 6.1 ) is flat under foot faults (66.6–67.6 mm; orientation faults never reach its inputs, and foot-acceleration dropout costs only + 1.0 +1.0 mm) and nominally beats the channel gate on clean data (66.6 vs. 69.4 mm; the edge persists under multi-view fused labels, supp. S2), but the comparison crosses trunks. Trunk- and recipe-matched on the gated architecture, the picture inverts: the a priori drop sits flat at 83.4 83.4 mm and the channel gate beats it on clean, drift, and dropout ( + 12.3 +12.3 / + 12.1 +12.1 / + 8.6 +8.6 mm, all p < 3 × 10 − 5 p{<}3{\times}10^{-5} ), with no detected difference under strong foot bias ( + 4.5 +4.5 [ − 1.5 , + 10.9 ] [-1.5,+10.9] , p = 0.17 p{=}0.17 ). The residual feet-A advantage is therefore a trunk/recipe effect, not a gating deficit. The decisive contrast is fault location: under head-stream dropout the a priori drop has no mechanism and collapses to 92.9 mm, while the channel gate partially closes the head-orientation gate inside the bursts ( 0.64 0.64 vs. 0.99 0.99 outside, seed s0, zero-shot since head faults are never trained) and holds 79.3 mm (HL + 13.1 +13.1 mm [ + 8.3 , + 18.1 ] [+8.3,+18.1] , p = 2 × 10 − 6 p{=}2{\times}10^{-6} ; matched trunk: + 16.2 +16.2 mm; supp. S4). Head faults are otherwise milder than foot faults at matched dose (ungated arm, eval-only uniform σ = 20 ∘ \sigma{=}20^{\circ} on both streams: median + 0.9 +0.9 mm head bias vs. + 3.8 +3.8 mm foot bias; per-joint breakdown: supp. S4), consistent with the foot orientation anchoring the distal kinematic chain.

blocks.en: Calibration is per-take, not one-time. A one-time mounting calibration fitted to each run’s opening T-pose segment is worse than no calibration at all (116.7 vs. 103.2 mm; HL + 18.3 +18.3 mm [ + 8.2 , + 26.9 ] [+8.2,+26.9] , p = 0.003 p{=}0.003 ), while full per-take calibration reaches 80.3 mm (supp. S4): a single static pose does not constrain the sensor-to-bone rotation tightly enough and locks in the residual error. Gating does not remove the need either: without per-take calibration head-only collapses to the mean-pose prior (105.5 mm) and ungated head+feet nearly does too (103.2 mm); the channel gate holds 94.0 mm (seed s0), the best camera-free arm tested but far short of calibrated head-only (79.0 mm; Table 1 ). Closing that gap without per-take vision is the deployment blocker (Sec. 7 ).

blocks.en: Failure modes. Per-motion and per-joint breakdowns (supp. S4, S6) localize the residual error on vertical motion, turning, and hip axial rotation (qualitative predictions: Fig. 3 , supp. S4). Gated fusion bounds the damage from unreliable channels but does not create information: under foot corruption the model falls back on head-dominated behavior, so the residual failure modes are those of the head-only model: geometric (vertical motion and turning; clean head-only R 2 R^{2} 0.06 0.06 , carried by the distal joints at 0.49 0.49 ; the channel gate lifts it to 0.24 0.24 ) and velocity-blind (every learned model trails the mean-pose prior on MPJVE, 220 vs. 253 mm/s; supp. S4, S6). A two-logit foot-contact head (BCE against SAM-derived contacts, trained jointly with the pose loss) reaches 0.809 macro-F1 ( + 0.02 +0.02 over always-contact), and causal unidirectional variants retain selectivity at a uniform accuracy cost (supp. S4). Drift remains the hardest fault to gate at stream level, since a slow random walk is locally indistinguishable from real motion over a 0.3 s window; the channel gate’s drift margin comes from suppressing the orientation block before drift accumulates, not from detecting drift itself [ 26 , 9 ] . Out-of-family probes (supp. S4): the trunk absorbs faults the gates do not detect (gain error, temporal shift, stale bursts), but white accelerometer noise, a fault in the trusted channel, degrades the gated model more than the ungated one ( 143 143 vs. 118 118 mm): the gates keep the noisy acceleration open and mis-attribute the fault. Learned trust allocation concentrates risk in the channels it trusts.

blocks.en: 7 Discussion and Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 讨论和结论

blocks.en: Consumer sensor reliability is a channel-level property: the same foot stream couples the most valuable signal (acceleration) with the most toxic one (fused orientation), and the standard remedies (augmentation without gating, oracle hard masking, one-time static calibration) all fail. Channel-reliability gating resolves this trade-off without test-time supervision. Limitations. All reference signals (alignment, labels, contacts, evaluation) derive from the same monocular model family, so millimeter claims are relative to SAM-3D-Body labels, not true anatomy; headline contrasts are paired on identical labels, so common-mode bias cancels, and residual interactions are partially bounded by the four-view control (Sec. 3 ) and gravity/depth audit (supp. S1). Temporal alignment is a per-take constant offset with no hardware sync; residual misalignment can mimic orientation-channel toxicity, and within-take drift is unmodeled (excluding low-confidence takes changes no conclusion, supp. S1). Further: one subject and day, so mechanistic claims plausibly transfer as device properties while millimeter numbers may not; synthetic corruptions; no pelvis sensor (root translation and torso orientation out of reach); per-take vision-derived mounting calibration; and a ∼ 6 {\sim}6 mm fusion-architecture cost the channel gate more than recovers. Consumer IMUs fail in ways fixed fusion cannot absorb; learning how much to trust each channel enables deployable capture.
